correctness.rationale: For ordered deviations u>v>=0 write the map as (A/B,|C|/D) with C=2v-u-uv. Both cross-product comparisons are positive, so the ordering persists even across the switching boundary. The larger coordinate decreases strictly within two steps away from the origin (including on the positive diagonal), which by compactness below the initial maximum implies collapse to zero. In the passive branch, C at the image is -2v(1-u)(3-u-v-uv)/(BD), so the exact wedge is invariant. If an orbit stayed in the active branch, after reaching u<=1/4 its relative separation (u-v)/u would grow by at least 39/32 every step, a contradiction. Substitution in the two-step map gives the relative factor 3/4+O(u) on each nonzero coordinate. Eventual geometric decay makes these relative errors summable, so the renormalized larger coordinate has a strictly positive limit, and the smaller has a limit (possibly zero). The one-step expansion on the wedge gives the stated odd amplitude; both parity maxima have positive leading coefficients. The diagonal's reciprocal recurrence gives the closed form, and the origin is fixed. This checks the continuous maxima map, not position-labelled tie-breaking. The supplied exact-rational check.py was inspected, not executed; replay is python3 check.py in the source package. Its finite checks are corroboration, not certification.
